panels.title: Health — is the pipeline OK at 3am?
Flink scrape targets up
panels.description: Number of Flink Prometheus endpoints (JobManager + TaskManager) Prometheus is successfully scraping. 0 means metrics are blind.

panels.title: Job restarts (per window)
panels.description: Full restarts of the streaming job within the selected time range (windowed increase of the cumulative counter). A flat 0 is healthy; a step shows exactly when a restart occurred so it can be correlated with load or checkpoint events.

panels.title: Failed checkpoints (per window)
panels.description: Checkpoints that failed within the selected time range (windowed increase). 0 during healthy operation; the benign one-time startup trigger-abort drops out because the lifetime counter stays flat. A nonzero step means checkpoints are failing now and is correlatable in time.

panels.title: Last checkpoint duration
panels.description: Duration of the most recent checkpoint over time (auto-scaled: ms for fast checkpoints, s for slow ones). A flat low line is healthy; a trend toward the 60s checkpoint timeout indicates backpressure or a slow write path.

panels.title: Kafka consumer lag — committed (Kafka) vs pending (Flink)
panels.description: Two views of how far behind ingest the pipeline is, on one axis so the gap is visible. 'committed lag (Kafka)' = latest - committed offset from kafka-exporter; Flink commits offsets only on a successful checkpoint, so this is the authoritative durable-progress signal and matches Kafka UI. 'pending records (Flink)' = latest - in-flight read position from Flink's own gauge, reported only while the source task is RUNNING. Healthy: both small, committed riding slightly above pending in a checkpoint-interval sawtooth. A widening gap (committed climbing while pending stays low or goes stale) means checkpoints are not completing, so offsets stop committing — the canonical 'are we keeping up' alarm, hence Health not Throughput.

panels.title: DLQ records / sec by stage
panels.description: Rate of dead-letter records emitted, broken down by the originating pipeline stage (PARSE, IMAGE_ENRICH, IMAGE_POSTGRES, DATA_POSTGRES, EVENT_TYPE_COUNT_POSTGRES). Backed by the custom dlq_records counter on the dlq-meter operator.

panels.title: Retryable enrichment failures / sec
panels.description: Rate of IMAGE enrichment failures classified as retryable (transient fetch/upload errors). Backed by the custom image_retryable_failures counter; retry pressure on the IMAGE branch.

panels.title: Backpressure & busy time (ms/s per task)
panels.description: Per-task time spent backpressured vs busy. Backpressure approaching 1000 ms/s means a downstream operator is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Throughput & performance — workload shape, not paging signals
Kafka consumer lag — committed (Kafka) vs pending (Flink)
panels.description: Mirror of the Health-row lag panel, stacked directly above events/sec so lag can be cross-referenced against throughput without leaving the Throughput view: rising committed lag while events/sec is flat means the pipeline, not the inbound rate, is the bottleneck. Both series (committed lag from kafka-exporter, pending records from Flink) share the Health-row panel's meaning; the paging-grade copy lives in the Health row.

panels.title: Average MinIO upload time (ms)
panels.description: Mean putObject duration over the window: rate(minio_upload_nanos) / rate(minio_uploads), converted to ms. Backed by the custom counter pair on the minio-enrich-async operator; only successful uploads are metered (idempotency hits and passthrough are excluded).

panels.title: Events / sec into Postgres by type (DATA vs IMAGE)
panels.description: Per-second records entering each Postgres write operator: data_to_postgres (DATA path) vs image_to_postgres (enriched IMAGE path). Reporter-native numRecordsIn, no custom code. Stacked between lag (above) and the cumulative-by-type counter (below) — the same numRecordsIn series as a rate. Permanent-write failures still count here; the per-stage DLQ panel in Health shows the failure split.

panels.title: MinIO uploads / sec
panels.description: Rate of successful MinIO putObject calls (custom minio_uploads counter). Distinct from IMAGE event rate: idempotency hits and backend-uploaded passthrough images do not perform a putObject and are not counted here.

panels.title: Cumulative events processed by type
panels.description: Running total of records entering each Postgres write operator since the job started. Same numRecordsIn series as events/sec (directly above), shown as the raw counter for the long-run DATA-vs-IMAGE workload mix. Resets to 0 on a job restart (expected).
